Why it matters

Clean air is a shared responsibility

Air pollution is the presence of harmful substances in the air that can affect human health, wildlife, and the environment. It reaches all of us, so the response has to as well.

About the project

Why we made this site

Breathe Clean, Live Green is an educational advocacy project for MO-ENV076 · People & Earth’s Ecosystems at Mapúa Malayan Digital College. It explains air pollution, the Philippine Clean Air Act, and practical solutions for healthier communities.

The air we share shapes the future we build.
How we handle facts

Our approach

Law and guidance first

We ground our work in RA 8749 and recognized guidance wherever possible.

A clear framework

Solutions are compared with Ekvall’s five criteria, not opinion alone.

Scores are labeled

Our scores are a group evaluation, not official ratings, and we say so.

Chapter 1 · The issue

Air pollution is more than what we see

From vehicle exhaust to industrial emissions and open burning, pollution has many sources.

🚗 Vehicles

Exhaust and fuel combustion release pollutants into the atmosphere.

🏭 Industries

Industrial processes and energy production can emit harmful substances.

🔥 Open burning

Burning waste produces smoke and toxic pollutants.

🏗️ Construction

Construction activity contributes dust and particulate matter.

The effects are far-reaching

Respiratory illness

Can worsen asthma and other breathing problems.

Heart health

Air pollution is linked to cardiovascular harm.

Climate impact

Some air pollutants contribute to climate change.

Ecosystems

Pollution can damage forests, water, and wildlife.

Chapter 2 · The Philippine response

RA 8749 — Philippine Clean Air Act of 1999

A framework for preventing and controlling air pollution, with the goal of protecting public health and the environment.

Read the law ↗

Air quality standards. Sets standards and guidelines to help protect air quality.

Emissions regulation. Addresses mobile and stationary sources.

Monitoring and programs. Supports monitoring, planning, and pollution-control programs.

Accountability. Provides penalties for violations.

Chapter 3 · Our selected solutions

Different solutions. One cleaner future.

Air pollution is complex, so our response should be too. These approaches can work together.

RA 8749 · Policy

Clean air regulations

Strengthen air-quality standards, emissions testing, monitoring, and accountability.

RA 9003 · Waste

Proper waste management

Improve segregation, collection, and recycling to prevent open burning.

Cleaner mobility

Sustainable transportation

Support public transport, walking and cycling, and cleaner fleets.

WHO · Clean energy

Global approaches

Use science-based guidance, renewable energy, and transparent monitoring.

Our position: prioritize stronger implementation and enforcement of RA 8749, while integrating waste management, sustainable transportation, and global approaches.

Our advocacy post

Breathe Clean, Live Green: 5 Simple Actions Against Air Pollution

Extra! Extra! Air pollution can feel like a huge problem, but everyday choices add up.

  1. Segregate, don’t burn. Open burning of solid waste is prohibited under RA 9003.
  2. Commute smart. Choose public transport, walking, or cycling when safe and practical.
  3. Maintain your vehicle. Well-maintained vehicles help reduce excessive emissions.
  4. Know and follow the law. The Clean Air Act (RA 8749) sets air-quality standards and regulates emissions.
  5. Speak up and share. Awareness starts with conversation.

No single solution is enough. Strong laws, proper waste management, and cleaner transportation work best together, with the participation of every community member.

Clean air is a shared responsibility.
